content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

The guidance: three steps: 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). 2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid (alkene) from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. 3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide bond to give acid and aniline (or amine). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aromatic ring (anilide). The amide is attached to the α,β-unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N... So the amide carbonyl is part of the chain: C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 1: disconnect amide to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid is something like Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1? Wait the acid is the α,β-unsaturated acid: /C=C/C(=O)N... Actually the amide carbonyl is attached to the unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl. So the acid precursor would be the α,β-unsaturated acid: /C=C/COOH attached to the aromatic sulfonamide ring? Let's parse target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have a tolyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) which has the α,β-unsaturated amide side chain. So the sulfonamide is between the tolyl amine (p-tolyl) and sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So step 3: sulfonamide formation: disconnect sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid derivative) and the tolyl amine (p-toluidine). So precursor: p-toluidine (C c1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide side chain.

Thus step 2: the unsaturated amide side chain is formed via amide coupling from unsaturated acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we need that acid precursor: the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to the second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2). That acid could be formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl with aldehyde) and malonic acid to give the α,β-unsaturated acid.

Thus step 2 (retrosynthesis) is to disconnect the amide, giving unsaturated acid and aniline. Step 2 (forward) is amide formation.

Step 1 (retrosynthesis) is to disconnect the unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid (Doebner). So we need aldehyde precursor: aromatic aldehyde attached to phenyl (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) with the sulfonyl group attached? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to that phenyl; the aldehyde is on that phenyl at the position where the unsaturated chain attaches. So the aldehyde is c2ccc(CHO) attached to sulfonyl group.

Thus overall route:

Target -> (retro) sulfonamide cleavage -> p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride bearing aldehyde side chain). Then the sulfonyl chloride precursor can be made from the corresponding sulfonic acid (maybe from sulfonyl chloride formation from sulfonic acid). But we can keep as sulfonyl chloride as a commercial reagent.

Then the aryl sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde side chain is made via amide coupling? Wait the aldehyde side chain is separate; the sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl ring; the aldehyde is on same phenyl ring. So we need to have that phenyl ring with both sulfonyl chloride and aldehyde substituents. That could be synthesized from a phenyl sulfonic acid (or sulfonyl chloride) and then formylation (e.g., Vilsmeier). But for retrosynthesis we can assume the sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde is available.

Thus three steps: 1) amide coupling (target from unsaturated acid + aniline). 2) Doebner modification (unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (target from p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride). However the sulfonamide formation is already step 3? Actually we need three reactions total. The order in forward synthesis: first sulfonamide formation (p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride) to give sulfonamide intermediate (aryl-sulfonyl attached to tolyl). Then Doebner modification to create unsaturated acid on the second phenyl? Wait the unsaturated acid is attached to the sulfonyl phenyl, not to the tolyl. So after sulfonamide formation, we have the sulfonamide attached to phenyl with aldehyde? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl that also will undergo Doebner to create unsaturated acid, then amide coupling to attach aniline. So forward order: start with p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (bearing aldehyde) -> sulfonamide intermediate (aryl-sulfonyl attached to tolyl). Then Doebner modification on the aldehyde (on same phenyl) with malonic acid to give α,β-unsaturated acid attached to sulfonamide. Then amide coupling with aniline to give final product.

Thus retrosynthetic order: target -> break amide -> unsaturated acid + aniline. Then unsaturated acid -> break to aldehyde + malonic acid. Then sulfonamide formation: break sulfonamide to p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (with aldehyde). So three steps.

Now we need to produce JSON route with type "mol" root target, children reaction nodes etc.

We need template IDs for each step. We have some templates from search results. For amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine) we have template ID 401931 (retro_smarts). That template corresponds to breaking amide to give acid and amine? The retro_smarts: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]'. This seems to break amide and alkene? Might be appropriate.

For Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid) we need a template that breaks C-C double bond formation etc. Not sure we have. Could search for functional groups broken: "C-C double bonds" formed? Actually forward Doebner forms C-C double bond, breaks C-C single bond (malonic acid decarboxylation) and C-O bond (aldehyde carbonyl). In retrosynthesis, we need to break the double bond to give aldehyde and malonic acid. So functional_groups_broken: "C-C double bonds". functional_groups_formed: "aldehydes", "carboxylic acids". Let's search.
